subject: POC MAP kickoff: evaluation roadmap & owners for MedFlow AI
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@medflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC MAP kickoff: evaluation roadmap & owners for MedFlow AI

Emily — thanks again for the productive call earlier. Per our conversation, I wanted to put the proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the POC in writing so everyone is aligned on success criteria, owners, and a pragmatic timeline. Attaching a lightweight MAP workbook and a short benchmark spec (stubs below).

High-level POC objective
- Validate Redwood's inference stack for MedFlow's clinical summarization pipeline at production latencies and quality that meet your acceptance bar.

Success criteria (proposed)
1) Quality: median ROUGE-L increase vs. current baseline >= +6 points on the clinical prompt set and hallucination rate <= 4% on red-team set.
2) Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for 512-token generation (med-svc traffic profile).
3) Cost: unit cost target <= $X per 1M input tokens (we'll confirm numbers on procurement).
4) Reliability: consistent throughput at target batch sizes with <1% error rate during a 24h soak test.

Benchmark plan (owners & brief scope)
- Prompt & eval harness (owner: Marissa Cole): build canonical prompt set (500 prompts: clinical notes, discharge summaries, Q/A), implement automated scoring (ROUGE/EM/hallucination checks).
- Infra & access (owner: Diego Fernandez): provision dedicated POC capacity, VPC peering, and log access; ensure KMS integration for test data.
- Implementation & tuning (owner: Rishi Malhotra): model configuration, batching/quantization experiments, coordinate rollouts.

Proposed timeline (dates are target / adjustable):
- Sep 6: Data & access complete (MedFlow provides sample corpus + test credentials).
- Sep 13: Baseline run + initial benchmark report.
- Sep 20–24: Focused tuning week (2 experiments: quantized variant + cache tuning).
- Sep 27: Final evaluation, scorecard review.
- Oct 4: Decision meeting (go/no-go / next steps).

Immediate asks from MedFlow:
- Primary POC stakeholders and a single Slack channel for day-to-day sync.
- A prioritized list of 1) critical prompts and 2) sensitive cases for red-team evaluation.

Attachments: MedFlow_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx), eval-benchmark-spec.md (text/markdown)

If this looks good I’ll upload the MAP workbook to the shared drive and schedule a 30-min kickoff for early next week.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182


From: Emily Chen <emily@medflow.ai>

Cc: Carlos Romero <carlos@medflow.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC MAP kickoff: evaluation roadmap & owners for MedFlow AI

Thanks Rishi — this is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few notes from our side: 

- Stakeholders: I (Emily) will be the POC owner; Carlos (VP Eng) will be the primary technical reviewer; Priya Shah (Clinical Lead) will own the clinical acceptability checks. I’ll add their emails to the shared folder.
- Success criteria: the ROUGE and hallucination thresholds look reasonable. For latency, can we also capture cold-start metrics (first token latencies) since we have bursty workloads at shift change?
- Data: we can share a 1k-sample de-identified set by Sep 3; for red-team cases, Priya will compile ~50 edge cases by Sep 10.

Quick ask: Can Marissa own a short prompt inventory template we can fill? That will speed up the prompt/harness work.

I’m good for a kickoff on Monday 9/7 at 10am PT — if that works for your team.

Best,
Emily
Emily Chen
Head of Product, MedFlow AI
emily@medflow.ai

Emily — happy to own the prompt & eval harness. I’ll drop a prompt inventory template and an example scoring notebook in the drive by EOD today. Quick clarifications from my side:

- Template: will include fields for input type, expected output format, clinical tags (ICD/LOINC where relevant), and manual accept/reject criteria for ambiguous cases.
- Scoring: will ship an automated pipeline that computes ROUGE-L, exact-match for extraction tasks, and a simple hallucination detector (keyword-based plus human review on uncertain flags).
- Timeline: Marissa will run an initial pass of 200 prompts immediately after we receive the sample corpus (target Sep 8).

Rishi — I’ll also coordinate with Diego on where to point the harness (endpoint + auth).

— Marissa
